status: Fitted to published mean values; no replicate-level data used

source_paper.title: KT-939: A Next-Generation Human Tyrosinase Inhibitor With Superior Efficacy for the Safe Management of Hyperpigmentation

verification.method: web fetch of PMC full-text HTML
verification.paper_quote_10uM: Following the washout of 10 μM KT-939, melanin inhibition rates were 66.6% and 52.7% on days 3 and 5, and 21.3% and 20% on days 7 and 9, respectively. Melanin content fully returned to normal levels after 11 days of drug withdrawal.
verification.paper_quote_1uM: After the washout of 1 μM KT-939, the melanin inhibition rate was 38% on day 3 and 28.3% on day 5, returning to baseline after seven days.
verification.transcription_notes: Percentages transcribed from publisher text fetched via PMC; values match those previously recorded in research/pigment-evidence-register.md line 120.

concentration_10_uM.condition: 10 μM KT-939 for 6 days, then washout with standard medium
concentration_10_uM.endpoint: bulk melanin content absorbance at 405 nm, normalized to protein (μg melanin / mg protein)
concentration_10_uM.inhibition_denominator: not explicit in paper; assumed percent of matched vehicle control
concentration_10_uM.replicates: three independent experiments (mean ± SD shown in Figure 4; exact SD per timepoint not reported in text)

concentration_1_uM.condition: 1 μM KT-939 for 6 days, then washout with standard medium

parameter_I0.description: extrapolated inhibition at t = 0 (immediately after washout, not measured)
parameter_I0.rationale: Single-exponential washout model; I0 is a fitted scaling parameter, not constrained to the 6-day exposure inhibition (~86.7% at 10 μM from Figure 3) because recovery may begin during the 6-day exposure or the first unmeasured post-washout interval.

parameter_k.rationale: Simplest kinetic model consistent with reversible suppression; assumes immediate switch to normal medium and no residual intracellular compound effect.

derived_half_time.caveat: This is a fitted parameter describing decay of accumulated-pigment-content inhibition, not a drug pharmacokinetic half-life, not a synthesis-flux recovery time, and not an iris cell turnover rate.

model.fit_series: 10 μM only; 1 μM is underdetermined (2 quantitative points for 2 parameters)

qualitative_recovery_bounds.description: day-11 (10 μM) and day-7 (1 μM) recovery statements are qualitative bounds, not 0% data points
qualitative_recovery_bounds.treatment_in_fit: excluded from least-squares objective; reported as bounds in MODEL_REPORT.md

underdetermined_series_treatment.concentration_1_uM: Two quantitative points cannot determine both I0 and k. The 1 μM series is reported as a bounding comparison only; no rate is fitted.

limitations_and_qualifications: The endpoint is accumulated pigment content (A405 per protein), not a direct synthesis-flux measurement. New synthesis, old-pigment turnover, cell division, and protein changes are confounded in this single readout.
The day-7 to day-9 plateau in the 10 μM series (21.3% -> 20.0% over 2 days) is inconsistent with a strict single exponential and must be flagged as a source inconsistency or experimental variability.
Exact SEM/SD per timepoint are not reported in the paper text; error bars visible in Figure 4 are not digitized here. The fit assumes equal weighting.
No replicate-level values are used; the fitted curve passes through means of three independent experiments.
Day 0 (immediately post-washout) and day 1 are not sampled; the fitted I0 is an extrapolation.
The model assumes no persistent non-zero inhibition floor. The qualitative day-11 recovery suggests the floor is near zero, but the model does not include it.
n=4 quantitative points for a 2-parameter nonlinear fit yields large uncertainty. Confidence intervals must be interpreted with this small-sample caveat.
MNT-1 melanoma cells are a transformed line, not normal human melanocytes or iris tissue. Rates do not transfer across cell types or tissues.
